# Exploratory Results

```{r, include= FALSE}
library("car")

library("ape")
```

## Model 0: Simple Model

```{r,include= FALSE}
library("pander")
simple_model <- readRDS("simple_model.rds")
results_m0 <- data.frame(
  effect = simple_model$effects$effectName,
  b = simple_model$theta,
  se = simple_model$se,
  t = simple_model$theta / simple_model$se,
  p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(simple_model$theta / simple_model$se))
)
```

The null model converges at 0.13, which is acceptable. The outcomes of
the simple model show things we have already learned from the
descriptive results and the network graph, namely that there is a
significant chance that one does not observe a tie compared to the
chance that one observes a tie (*b* = -2.67, *SE* = 0.53, *p* \> .01).

The rate for the behavioural is significant, meaning that... Change in
social satisfaction is not significant on a linear level (*b* = 0.17,
*SE* = 0.14, *p* = 0.22), but it is significant on a quadratic level
(*b* = -0.34, *SE* = 0.15, *p =* 0.02) and going into a negative
direction, which indicates that ...

However, these statistics do not tell me a lot yet, as I have not added
it any additional statistics. Because of that, the Goodness-Of-Fit
models for this model will indicate that the models do not fit well.
Therefore, I will not plot them yet.

**Table 1:** *Results of Model 0*

```{r}
pander::pander(results_m0)
```

## Model 1: Homogeneity in Reciprocated Ties

```{r, include= FALSE}
model1 <- readRDS("model1.rds")
results_m1 <- data.frame(
  effect = model1$effects$effectName,
  b = model1$theta,
  se = model1$se,
  t = model1$theta / model1$se,
  p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(model1$theta / model1$se))
)
```

The first model is used to look at whether reciprocated ties are more likely to occur among students whose parents have the same educational level. 


```{r}
results_m1
```


**Table 2:** *Results of Model 1*

```{r}
pander::pander(results_m1)
```

```{r, include= FALSE}
gofi1 <- sienaGOF(model1, IndegreeDistribution, verbose = FALSE, join = TRUE, varName = "netMLC")
gofo1 <- sienaGOF(model1, OutdegreeDistribution, verbose = FALSE, join = TRUE, varName = "netMLC")
gof1tc <- sienaGOF(model1, TriadCensus, verbose = FALSE, join = TRUE, varName = "netMLC")
```

```{r, include= FALSE}
#Loading the data
rm(list =ls())
load("C:\\Users\\ninas\\OneDrive - Radboud Universiteit\\RSCS\\Social Networks\\labjournalSN\\parentedudata.Rdata")
load("C:\\Users\\ninas\\OneDrive - Radboud Universiteit\\RSCS\\Social Networks\\labjournalSN\\wave1.Rdata")
load("C:\\Users\\ninas\\OneDrive - Radboud Universiteit\\RSCS\\Social Networks\\labjournalSN\\wave2.Rdata")
```

```{r}
#dependent variable 
netMLC <- sienaDependent(array(data = c(wave1, wave2), dim = c(dim(wave1), 2)))
#behavioural variable
behy <- df2 %>% 
  dplyr::select("socsatw1n", "socsatw2n") %>%
  as.matrix()
behMLC <- sienaDependent(behy, type = c("behavior"))
#independent variables
parent_edu_ccv <- coCovar(as.numeric(df2$parentshighf))
gender_ccv <- coCovar(as.numeric(df2$genderf))
ethnicity_ccv <- coCovar(as.numeric(df2$ethnicityf))
#data
mydata <- sienaDataCreate(netMLC, behMLC, parent_edu_ccv, gender_ccv, ethnicity_ccv)
#effects structure
myeff <- getEffects(mydata)
#?
myAlgorithm <- (sienaAlgorithmCreate(projname = "results"))
```

## Model 0: Simple Model

```{r, eval= FALSE}
simple_model <- siena07(myAlgorithm, data = mydata, effects = myeff, thetaBound = 10000, returnDeps = T)
```

## Model 1: Homogeneity in reciprocated ties

```{r, include= FALSE}
#goodness of fit practicalities
GeodesicDistribution <- function(i, data, sims, period, groupName, varName, levls = c(1:5, Inf), cumulative = TRUE,
    ...) {
    x <- networkExtraction(i, data, sims, period, groupName, varName)
    require(network)
    require(sna)
    a <- sna::geodist(symmetrize(x))$gdist
    if (cumulative) {
        gdi <- sapply(levls, function(i) {
            sum(a <= i)
        })
    } else {
        gdi <- sapply(levls, function(i) {
            sum(a == i)
        })
    }
    names(gdi) <- as.character(levls)
    gdi
}

# The following function is taken from the help page for sienaTest

testall <- function(ans) {
    for (i in which(ans$test)) {
        sct <- score.Test(ans, i)
        cat(ans$requestedEffects$effectName[i], "\n")
        print(sct)
    }
    invisible(score.Test(ans))
}
```

```{r}
myeff <- includeEffects(myeff, egoX, altX, sameX, sameXRecip, interaction1 = "parent_edu_ccv") 
model1.1 <- siena07(myAlgorithm, data = mydata, effects = myeff, thetaBound = 10000, returnDeps = T)
model1.1
```

```{r}
gofi1.1 <- sienaGOF(model1.1, IndegreeDistribution, verbose = FALSE, join = TRUE, varName = "netMLC")
gofo1.1 <- sienaGOF(model1.1, OutdegreeDistribution, verbose = FALSE, join = TRUE, varName = "netMLC")

```

```{r}
plot(gofi1.1)
plot(gofo1.1)
plot(gof1.1.tc, center = T, scale = T)
```

WELL, that does not very good. But that's not weird, because I have not
added any additional effects. Let's add a triad effect :)

## Model 2: Homogeneity in reciprocated ties with control variables
